post.description:
Analyse a product web page for legitimacy using the LangGraph analysis pipeline, paid from the account's credits.

Passes the page (client-supplied facts and/or HTML or cleaned text) through the graph, which extracts the
facts, runs the cheap skills in parallel, lets the triage decide on expensive ones, then synthesises a
reliability score, an explanation and the shopper verdict (in the ``Accept-Language`` language). The analysis
price is taken from the balance up front and refunded when the page can't be analysed (score -1) or the
analysis fails. The same input analysed again within the hour is served from an in-memory cache, free of
charge. Nothing about the page or the result is stored; the ``report_token`` lets the caller report a wrong
result later (``POST /v1/reports``), sharing the page only then and only with their consent.

The caller is a wallet's session (``Authorization: Bearer <session token>``) or an API key (``Bearer ufk_…``).

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param address: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: Reliability score (0–100), explanation, verdict, the scorer's assessment, the balance left and a
    report token.
:raises InternalServerError: If the graph fails.
:raises GatewayTimeoutError: If the analysis takes longer than ``analysis_timeout_s``.
:raises asyncio.CancelledError: If the client hung up (after the refund).

Analyse a page like ``POST /v1/analyze``, streaming progress as server-sent events while skills finish.

Events: one ``step`` per finished node (``{"skill", "findings"}`` with the finding types, plus ``page_type``
once classified), then a final ``result`` (the ``POST /v1/analyze`` body, with all the evidence) or ``error``.
Charged like ``POST /v1/analyze``: free on a cache hit (the result comes at once), refunded on ``error``, a score
of -1, or when the client hangs up before the analysis finished. A finished result is cached first, so a client
that lost the connection gets it again for free by repeating the request.

:param body: The request body containing the page content and flags.
:param request: The FastAPI request (used to access the compiled graph).
:param address: The account (injected by require_account).
:return: A ``text/event-stream`` response.

With ``pair`` (a phone pairing), the statement names the pairing's confirmation code, and ``/verify`` only
accepts that exact statement for that pairing.

:param request: The incoming request.

:return: The sign-in input.

post.description:
Start a phone sign-in for the extension: a pairing id, its confirmation code and the URL to open on the phone.

The pairing lives five minutes in memory. The extension shows ``connect_url`` as a QR code and the code next to
it, then polls ``GET /v1/auth/pair/{pair_id}``.

:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The pairing.
:raises TooManyRequestsError: If this visitor started too many pairings (or the server holds too many).

:param pair_id: The pairing id.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: 200 with the session (then the pairing is gone), or 202 while waiting.
:raises GoneError: If the pairing expired before anyone signed in.
:raises NotFoundError: If the pairing is unknown (or its session was already collected).

What the phone shows before signing: the confirmation code to compare with the computer's screen.

:param pair_id: The pairing id from the connect URL.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The code and the pairing's expiry.

post.description:
Finish a sign-in: check the signed message and return a session token.

The signature only proves control of the wallet; it grants no spending rights. A wallet's first sign-in may
come with the free trial (only for wallets with on-chain history).

:param body: The signed message.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The session.
:raises UnauthorizedError: If the message or signature is not acceptable.

Retrying with the same payment returns the same answer (for 15 minutes) and is never charged twice.

:param body: URL, optional page HTML, tier and policy.
:param request: The incoming request (payment header, app state).
:return: The verdict, or an x402 payment-required / error response.

post.description:
Start a card (or other fiat) payment that tops up an API key, at the provider's hosted checkout.

The provider handles the buyer's details, invoice and tax; this service only learns that the key was paid for.
Credited when the provider's webhook confirms the payment, with the same bonus tiers as crypto.

:param body: The key and the amount.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The checkout URL.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: While no fiat provider is configured.
:raises BadRequestError: If the amount is out of range.

Build the unsigned SOL or USDC transfer that buys credits; the buyer's wallet signs and sends it.

Credits arrive once the transfer is finalized (about 15–30 seconds): its dollar value (SOL converted at crediting
time, USDC exact) plus any bonus tier that value reaches, credited to the beneficiary named in the transaction's
memo (the paying wallet unless ``beneficiary`` or ``key_id`` says otherwise). No sign-in needed: anyone may fund
any wallet or API key.

:param body: Who buys how much, in which currency.
:param request: The incoming request.
:return: The transaction (base64) and a Solana Pay link for phone wallets.

post.description:
Report that a result is wrong. With ``consent``, this one check's page data is shared for review.

Send back the ``report_token`` from the result with the request and explanation exactly as they were, so the
report provably concerns a check this account got. Personal details are scrubbed before anything is stored.
A page already in the queue counts the report as confirmation; a page reviewed recently is ``already_known``.
If the review shows the score was far off (30+ points outside the label's zone), the first reporter gets free
checks. Limits: a few reports per account per month, one per page.

:param body: The report.
:param request: The incoming request.
:param account: The reporting account (injected by require_account).
:return: The outcome.
:raises ServiceUnavailableError: If reports are off (no session secret) or the queue is full.
